std: Explain how the rules help us work together.
Interact with a variety of primary and secondary sources.
Demonstrate an awareness of community leaders (teacher, principal, mayor, tribal leaders).
Compare traditions found in communities over time.
Recognize and identify signs and symbols around their town and community including the locations of places, people, and objects.
Identify authority figures and describe their roles.
Use a variety of maps to locate specific places and identify major landforms, bodies of water, and other places of significance around the United States.
Explain and provide examples of how people play important roles in society.
Examine how earning money through work is related to the purchase of goods and services.

Create geographic representations to identify the location of familiar places and demonstrate how these representations can help us navigate from one place to the next, provide directions, or trace important routes.
Take group or individual action to help address local, regional, and/or global problems or issues.
Investigate how people work together to accomplish a common task and how this benefits and challenges people when working together.
Investigate significant events, people, and observances in history and discuss their effects on local and national communities.
Examine and identify cultural differences within their community.
Examine choices that families make in purchasing general goods and identify costs associated with these choices.
Identify the common symbols used on maps for human-made structures and physical features.
Understand the purposes and structures of government (tribal, local, state, national government).
Using maps, identify and locate the United States, Canada, and Mexico as the countries that make up North America.
Identify examples of producers and consumers.
Assess how the contributions of diverse individuals’ have helped develop our national identity.
Compare the human and physical characteristics of two regions in the United States.
Identify the actions of people and groups who have worked throughout history to improve their community which then leads to a more equitable society.
Identify and explain the structure and function of the three branches of government and how they form the basis for our constitutional and federal republic.
Apply geographic tools of title, grid system, legends, symbols, scale and compass rose to construct and interpret digital and analog maps.
Explain how the principles of the founding documents and the principle of liberty became unifying ideas of American democracy.
